routing protocol. Every router in an area learns the full map of that area (who is connected to whom). Each router then runs the
algorithm on that map to find the best path to every network, and puts those paths in its routing table. This is different from RIP, where routers only pass around distances and never see the map.
Open standard: works between vendors (but see the warning on cost later).
Fast convergence, and it supports equal-cost multipath (several equal best routes).
Supports VLSM / CIDR and has no hop-count limit.
Sends updates only when something changes (event-triggered) and uses areas to keep updates small.
Supports IPv4 (OSPFv2) and IPv6 (OSPFv3, a separate version of the protocol).

a group of contiguous networks and routers that share the same map. Areas cut routing overhead, speed up convergence and keep a problem inside one area.
